concept: replSetResizeOplog and oplog compaction on self-managed replica sets

claims.text: replSetResizeOplog changes do not replicate. Connect directly to each intended member and process secondaries before the primary, as the official resizing procedure directs. (high confidence)

Run db.adminCommand({replSetResizeOplog:1,size:Double(16000)}) on the target self-managed member to set a 16000 MB logical oplog maximum without restarting mongod; unscaled local.oplog.rs.stats().maxSize reports bytes. (high confidence)

Reducing the oplog limit does not automatically return allocated disk space. MongoDB prescribes db.getSiblingDB('local').runCommand({compact:'oplog.rs'}) to reclaim unused space after a reduction; its tutorial says compaction provides no benefit after increasing the limit. (high confidence)

The configured oplog size is not an absolute disk ceiling: retaining the majority commit point can exceed it, and minRetentionHours can preserve entries beyond the size limit until they age out. (high confidence)

Run db.adminCommand({replSetResizeOplog:1,size:Double(16000)}) to set one self-managed member's oplog limit to 16000 MB without restarting mongod. The change does not propagate to other members. (high confidence)

MongoDB's resizing procedure handles secondaries first and the primary last. Inspect db.getSiblingDB('local').oplog.rs.stats().maxSize to verify the configured limit; unscaled maxSize is in bytes. (high confidence)

Perform compaction separately on each required member, preferring secondaries; step down the old primary before compacting it. Compaction is not replicated. Check reclaimed space rather than assuming command success guarantees filesystem reduction. (high confidence)
Shrinking can truncate history needed by lagging secondaries, change streams, or mongodump --oplog; check reader progress before reducing it. (low confidence)

For self-managed maintenance, compact secondaries sequentially, step down the old primary, and compact it after it becomes a secondary. The compact command itself does not replicate. (high confidence)

Compaction attempts to reclaim obsolete blocks; block availability and placement determine effectiveness, and it can need additional free space. Compare storage statistics before and after and monitor mongod logs or db.currentOp(). (medium confidence)

An independent operator transcript changes oplog maxSize from 2147483648 to 1073741824 bytes and then reports bytesFreed:49152 from compact. This is an unversioned observation, not evidence that shrinking by 1 GiB returns 1 GiB to the filesystem. (low confidence)

Percona reports replication and reads while compacting the ordinary collection test.demo on PSMDB 6.0.14-11. Its displayed replication entries fall within the compaction interval, but its displayed read timestamp precedes that interval; the read transcript therefore does not independently demonstrate concurrent reads. This experiment does not directly test local.oplog.rs compaction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-07-17)

The general compact reference permits secondary replication starting in 6.0.2/6.1.0; SERVER-68694 records removal of oplog-application blocking with fixes also listed for 4.4.17 and 5.0.12. These are general command changes, not an oplog-collection-specific availability test. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-07-17)
The autoCompact reference explicitly excludes an existing oplog from background compaction; enabling background compaction therefore does not establish oplog disk reclamation. (low confidence)

For authenticated oplog compaction, verify the compact action on local.oplog.rs. The general compact reference prescribes a custom role for system collections; its ordinary dbAdmin and hostManager guidance is explicitly for non-system collections. (medium confidence)

Shrinking history can strand lagging secondaries or consumers. MongoDB warns of secondary resynchronization and change-stream invalidation; Stitch documents full collection rereplication after its saved oplog position ages out. (high confidence)

MongoDB's general compact reference permits secondary replication and reads starting in 6.0.2 and 6.1.0. SERVER-68694 records fixes in 4.4.17, 5.0.12, 6.0.2 and 6.1.0-rc0. These statements alone do not resolve oplog-specific synchronization behavior. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Percona's July 2024 demonstration used PSMDB 6.0.14-11 and compacted test.demo while replication continued. It did not compact local.oplog.rs, so it is not a direct test of oplog compaction concurrency. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-07-17)

autoCompact, introduced in MongoDB 8.0, explicitly excludes the oplog from background compaction. Enabling it therefore does not replace explicit local.oplog.rs compaction after shrinking an oplog. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

compact attempts block reclamation; effectiveness depends on free-block placement and it may need additional disk space. MongoDB 8.0 adds dryRun for estimating reclaimable bytes before actual compaction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
